newsitem.title: USA: SALT RIVER PROJECT ACQUIRES 200 MW SUMMER POWER.
newsitem.headline: SALT RIVER PROJECT ACQUIRES 200 MW SUMMER POWER.

text.p: Arizona-based Salt River Project (SRP) announced Wednesday two 100 megawatt (MW) diversity exchange agreements to acquire summer season power from Louisville Power Marketing Inc. and U.S. Generating Co.
The deals, which require no cash expense, are valued at around $30 million over the length of the four-year contracts, SRP said.
Under the terms, Kentucky-based Louisville Power will provide SRP with 100 megawatt hours (MWh) during on-peak hours from June through September for four years beginning in 1998.
In exhange, SRP said it will deliver 83 MWh of peak power to Louisville Power from October through March for four years beginning this year.
In a separate deal, U.S. Generating, based in Bethesda, Md., will provide SRP with 100 MWh during peak demand hours from July through September for four years beginning in 1999.
SRP will deliver 46 MWh of "flat product" (all hours) to U.S. Generating from October through March for four years beginning in 1999.
All of the deliveries in the exchange agreements will take place at the Palo Verde switchyard west of Phoenix, SRP said.

"Our projections show that with no future increase in generating capacity, SRP will soon need additional resources during the summer months to meet customer needs," said Dave Slick, SRP's manager of strategic asset management, in a statement.
"These diversity exchange agreements help address this concern, while also helping SRP make better use of its excess capacity during the winter months," he added.
SRP is the third-larges public power utility in the U.S., serving more than 650,000 customers in the Phoenix area.
